sources.note: Glottolog lists 6 refs, none descriptive (Ethnologue 17; four Masalit items mis-assigned by computer; the 1995 SIL survey). Wikidata/Wikipedia carry Ethnologue data only. CrossRef 0 hits; archive.org catalogue only Wikipedia dumps.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2021 (draft 10 Jan 2021). The Maban languages and their place within Nilo-Saharan. Cambridge: unpublished ms, 25 pp.
sources.note: Surbakhal appears only in Table 1 (Ouaddaï, Assoungha, 7,890 speakers 2000) and the classification tree; sec. 2.3 says knowledge of such varieties comes only from unpublished SIL survey reports (Maass, Grant & Prinz 1995). Sec. 4.3 Tones covers Maba and Aiki only. No Surbakhal data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: SIL International, Language & Culture Archives listing for Surbakhal [sbj] (Wayback snapshot 2015-09-18)
sources.note: Catalogue listing only: exactly one item exists for sbj, the Maass/Grant/Prinz 1995 survey report (entry 4877). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Maass, Antje, Angela Prinz & Caroline Grant. 1996. Rapport d'enquête sociolinguistique: première évaluation parmi les Kendedje du Ouaddaï. N'Djamena: Association SIL. ii+12 pp.
sources.note: Sibling report from the same January-1995 trip; contains the Sourbakhal wordlist comparison (Sourbakhal/Massalit 74% ±3.4, Sourbakhal/Kendedje 69-70%, Sourbakhal/Maba 56%; App. B) and the Jan-1995 Sourbakhal group questionnaire (App. C). No phonology; nothing on stress, tone or accent.

sources.citation: Edgar, John. 1989. A Masalit grammar, with notes on other languages of Darfur and Wadai. Berlin: Reimer (Rosetta Project extracts 'Masalit Phonology' and 'Masalit Detailed Description', scanned text)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan): WID Offsite Storage PL8475.1.E34 1989 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Describes MASALIT (nucl1440), not Surbakhal; Surbakhal is not mentioned. Sec. 3.0 TONE: Maba-group languages 'would appear to have at least two phonemic tones... true for Masalit (high tone, low tone, falling tone, rising tone and downsteps are present)'; study based on the southern (Sudan) dialect. Nothing on stress. Context only.

sources.citation: Maass, Antje, Caroline Grant & Angela Prinz. 1995. Rapport d'enquête sociolinguistique: première évaluation parmi les sourbakhal du ouaddai. N'djamena: Association SIL. 12 pp. + 6 appendixes (SIL archive entry 4877)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only work devoted to Surbakhal; contains the wordlist the lexical-similarity figures rest on. Sibling 1996 Kendeje report has no phonology, so a stress statement is unlikely, but it is the sole primary document and its appendixes may print the transcribed wordlist (possibly tone-marked).

sources.citation: Edgar, John T. 1991. Maba-group lexicon (Sprache und Oralität in Afrika 13). Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. 426 pp.

sources.note: Most comprehensive compilation of Maba-group lexical data (per Blench 2021), synthesising unpublished material; may contain Surbakhal/western-Masalit forms and introductory remarks on prosody. Coverage of Surbakhal unverified.
